name: Universal IDs: UID2, ID5, RampID
plain: Shared advertising IDs derived from login email so ad partners can match people without cookies.
meaning: A publisher sends a hashed or encrypted email at login; the ID vendor returns a token that ad platforms accept. UID2 (The Trade Desk, open source), ID5 and LiveRamp RampID let a person be recognised across sites and apps whenever they log in.

web.api: Publisher JS SDK (UID2 SDK, ID5 API, LiveRamp ATS) and server APIs

access.persistence: Tokens rotate; UID2 advertising tokens are short lived with refresh tokens valid for days to weeks (verify per vendor docs)
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can give you a shared ad ID based on your login email, with no cookie
limits.user_action: You sign in or give your email on a site that joins the system
can: Turn your email into a shared ad ID
Let many ad partners recognize you with the same ID
Keep recognizing you after you clear cookies
cannot: Create an ID without you giving an email or logging in
Reach you on sites that do not take part
Stay the same if you use a different email
Give out your plain email; it uses a scrambled version, and some systems let you opt out
limits.reach_label: A stable ID across many sites

story.what_it_is: Shared ad IDs built from your login email so ad partners can match you without cookies.

marketing.name: Unified ID 2.0
marketing.pitch: UID2 is pitched as an open, email based ID for ad targeting after cookies, with opt out for people.

story.for_you: You log in to a site with your email. The site may turn it into a token that ad partners accept. You do not see it, and it can follow you across sites and apps each time you log in.
story.for_makers: Cookies are fading, so ad buyers want a stable login based ID. A publisher sends a hashed email, gets a token and sells it to ad buyers. Logged in audiences earn higher ad prices.

use_cases.example: A news site shares a UID2 token at login so advertisers can find you again on a streaming service.
A streaming service uses a login email token to match viewers to ads on TV and phones.
A game portal with logins sends a token so ad buyers can reach the same player on web and mobile.
An advertiser measures reach across publishers using one ID, instead of counting the same person twice.
A retailer matches its customer list to an ID graph, to find them on other sites.
People can opt out on the vendor site, but few know of it.

risks: Follows you across sites and apps

technical_bounds: Requires a user supplied email or phone
Opt-out portals exist (for example UID2 transparency and controls at transparentadvertising.org)
Raw email is not in the token but hashing is reversible by dictionary attack on guessable emails

abuse: Stable lifetime identifier tied to a real email
Matching offline data to online browsing

history.change: Google confirmed third-party cookies stay, so email based IDs complement rather than replace cookies
